text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.4% today as oil prices remained supported by geopolitical tensions and supply concerns. Brent crude—the global benchmark—topped $106 a barrel yesterday following a deadly attack on a Saudi airport, and ongoing conflict in the Middle East (Saudi-Houthi tensions, Iran fortifying nuclear sites) continues to raise the prospect of supply disruptions. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to stronger profits, and the stock has gained 12% over two weeks as oil has remained elevated.

The current price environment reflects a tug-of-war: while some relief is expected from potential Russian diesel entering global markets and political pressure to lower fuel costs, the underlying geopolitical risks in the Middle East keep a floor under crude prices and support the energy sector broadly.
